title: Adaptive invocation specs and SDK usage examples for progressive streaming + tool interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a compact, language-agnostic invocation contract and provides concrete TypeScript, Python, and Go SDK examples that demonstrate: 1) progressive streaming of model output as typed events, 2) robust tool/function calling with resumable and idempotent invocation semantics, and 3) thin compatibility shims so existing customers can upgrade with minimal changes. The goal is to enable developers to adopt streaming + tool-calls with predictable error modes and straightforward migration paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec doc describing event-envelope format, framing rules, and lifecycle states (started, partial, tool-call, resumed, completed, error) reviewed by runtime and SDK leads. 2) Minimal TS + Py + Go examples that implement the spec and are included in the SDK repo examples/adapter-compatible/ directory. 3) E2E smoke test (local runtime) that validates tool-call roundtrip and resumption. 4) Migration guide and FAQ published in the SDK docs. 5) Design review signoff and PRs opened for each language with CI.
design_notes:
We chose an event-envelope approach (lightweight envelope per emitted fragment) to keep compatibility with existing streaming clients while enabling typed structured outputs and explicit tool-call boundaries. Key trade-offs considered:
- Per-event JSON envelope increases token overhead vs raw chunk streaming but provides deterministic parsing for multi-language SDKs.
- We require a stable 'session_id' header to support resumable sessions; that implies small changes in hosted runtime (see ENG-4821).
- Tool calls are encoded as explicit 'tool_request' / 'tool_response' events; SDKs surface these as async callbacks to avoid blocking the main token stream.
- Backpressure and client buffer semantics: SDKs will provide both a high-level async iterator (TS/Py) and a lower-level event callback API for advanced users.
- Error handling: we codify 'retryable' vs 'fatal' errors in the envelope to allow automatic resumption when safe.
interface_sketch_py:
Python minimal interfaces (for discussion):

class Envelope(TypedDict, total=False):
    session_id: str
    seq: int
    type: str  # 'start','partial','tool_request','tool_response','complete','error','keepalive'
    payload: Any
    retryable: bool

class ProgressiveInvocation:
    def __init__(self, ...): ...
    def stream(self) -> AsyncIterator[Envelope]: ...
    async def cancel(self): ...
    def resume(self, session_id: str) -> 'ProgressiveInvocation': ...

# Example consumer
async for ev in client.invoke_progressive(prompt):
    if ev['type'] == 'partial':
        print(ev['payload'], end='')
    elif ev['type'] == 'tool_request':
        await run_tool(ev['payload'])
sdk_examples_summary: Provided examples will cover three migration scenarios: 1) 'lift-and-run' where existing non-streaming users call the same client.invoke(...) but receive a single 'complete' envelope — minimal changes. 2) 'progressive upgrade' where users get partial tokens via async iterators and can opt into tool-call callbacks. 3) 'advanced' where users implement resumable sessions for long-running prompts or intermittent mobile connectivity. Each example includes a short README and CI smoke tests.

- Performance microbench: measure overhead per-envelope (average bytes) and end-to-end latency for small partial fragments.
- Add e2e in release candidate CI gating for sdk-2026.04.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: customers using raw streaming parsers may break when envelopes are introduced. Mitigation: provide a compatibility mode where the server can emit raw chunks and a header 'X-RWD-Envelope: disabled' and publish a migration tutorial.
Risk: increased per-event overhead causing cost-sensitive customers to avoid streaming. Mitigation: recommend chunk-size tuning and batching heuristics; Redwood Optimize will include suggestions.
Risk: tool-call lifecycles may introduce blocking; mitigation: SDK will surface tool_request as non-blocking callback by default and provide helper patterns for sync wrappers.
next_steps: 1) Merge TS/Go/Py PRs after addressing ordering tests (target 03/18). 2) Publish migration guide and run internal 'dogfood' against Console features that render token streams. 3) Coordinate with runtime (ENG-4821) to enable session_id passthrough in hosted API. 4) Collect developer feedback via a small alpha program (10 customers) to validate ergonomics and cost metrics.
notes_for_engineering:
- Keep envelope parsing zero-copy where possible (Go/Py) to minimize GC overhead.
- Ensure SDK telemetry emits envelope sequence gaps for observability (Console can highlight missing seqs).
- Add a feature flag in SDKs to toggle 'envelope_mode' for early experimentation.
- Validate cross-language examples during the CI job using the runtime dev image.
